title: Predicting Metastatic Risk from Primary Cancer Tissue Architecture via Distance-Aware Spatial Modeling
abstract: arXiv:2606.28676v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Predicting distant metastasis from the digital H & E slides of the primary tumor is a critical yet challenging task in computational pathology. Multiple Instance Learning (MIL) approaches can attend to subdomains in whole slide images (WSIs) that harbor features of pre-metastatic cancer regions. However, conventional MIL models largely treat tissue patches as unordered bags, discarding the spatial layout that defines how these regions are arranged and interact across the tissue. We propose that metastatic risk is shaped not only by local patch appearance, but also by the geometric organization of patches in the WSI and the interaction between the tissue compartments. To this end, we introduce Distance-aware Tissue Modeling for Multiple Instance Learning (DTMF-MIL), a spatial MIL framework that reinforces feature embeddings with explicit distance priors. translated_title: 基于距离感知空间建模从原发癌组织结构预测转移风险
translated_abstract: 从原发肿瘤的数字化H&E切片预测远处转移是计算病理学中一项关键但具有挑战性的任务。多示例学习（MIL）方法能够关注全切片图像（WSI）中包含转移前癌症区域特征的子区域。然而，传统的MIL模型在很大程度上将组织斑块视为无序的集合，丢弃了定义这些区域如何在组织中排列和相互作用的空间布局。我们提出，转移风险不仅由局部斑块的外观决定，还由斑块在WSI中的几何组织以及组织区室之间的相互作用所决定。为此，我们提出了面向多示例学习的距离感知组织建模（DTMF-MIL），这是一个空间MIL框架，通过显式的距离先验来增强特征嵌入。通过计算有符号距离函数（SDF）来捕获具有相似特征的区域……（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 提出DTMF-MIL空间多示例学习框架，通过有符号距离函数将显式距离先验融入特征嵌入，从原发肿瘤H&E全切片中预测转移风险，弥补了传统MIL忽略组织空间布局信息的缺陷。
en_tdlr: DTMF-MIL is a spatial multiple instance learning framework that reinforces feature embeddings with explicit distance priors via signed distance functions to predict metastatic risk from primary tumor H&E whole slide images, addressing conventional MIL's neglect of spatial tissue layout.
